request.spec:
While an as-of date is set, the roles shown on the screen are those in force at the end of that
day.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
While an as-of date is set, the roles shown on the screen are those in force at the end of that
day.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The roles list now shows the roles that applied at the end of the as-of day, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**The roles change (server only):**
- The app already kept a dated record every time a role was set, and roles set before that history existed were copied in at the start. Nothing new needed storing.
- `RoleRevisionRepository` gets a query for a sheet's role records up to a given day.
- `RoleService.listOn(sheetId, day)` takes the last role given to each user on or before that day. A user who had no role yet by then isn't listed.
- `GET /api/sheets/{id}/roles` (in `RoleController`) uses this when the screen sends an as-of date. Without one, it answers exactly as before.
- No front-end change was needed. The screen already sends the as-of date with every request and re-reads the roles when it changes.

**A second change you didn't ask for.** Scenario 3 failed on an audit line that has nothing to do with roles. The spec expects `PERSON_EDITED … grade=B terms=3` when an edit leaves the person's own terms in force. The app only wrote `terms=` when the terms themselves changed. I changed `PersonService` so `PERSON_EDITED` also writes `terms=<n>` whenever the person has their own terms in force on the sheet's today, the same way `PERSON_ADDED` already does. Every other `PERSON_EDITED` line in the spec is for a person without their own terms, so those lines are unchanged. The same save code runs when people are merged, so a merged person with their own terms will now get `terms=` on that line too.
